title: A New Robust Constraint on the Self-interaction Cross-section of Dark Matter with Double Radio Relic Clusters
summary: Merging galaxy clusters are a promising laboratory for measuring the self-interaction cross-section (SICS) of dark matter. However, previous studies have focused on galaxy-mass offsets, which numerical simulations have shown to be intrinsically small because galaxies remain tightly coupled to the dominant dark matter potential even with significant self-interaction. Their interpretation is further complicated by unknowns of the merger phase, geometry, and initial conditions. In this paper, we overcome these obstacles by introducing the shock-to-shock distance, traced by double radio relics, as a merger chronometer that time-stamps the post-pericenter dynamical phase. Because the propagation speed of merger shocks is nearly independent of the SICS, while the halo-to-halo distance is depressed by SIDM-induced drag, the ratio of the two distances translates directly into a constraint on sigma/m. Applying this method to a gold sample of eleven cluster mergers hosting symmetric double radio relics, we determine a 68% upper limit on the SICS of sigma/m < 0.22 cm^2/g. This is the first constraint from cluster collisions that fully marginalizes over mass uncertainty, viewing angle, collision speed, merger phase, impact parameter, and gas profile slope.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a novel technique using shock-to-shock distances in merging galaxy clusters to robustly constrain the self-interaction cross-section of dark matter, obtaining a stringent upper limit of sigma/m < 0.22 cm^2/g while accounting for key uncertainties in merger dynamics.
AI.motivation: Previous measurements of SICS from galaxy-mass offsets have been intrinsically limited and complicated by merger phase, geometry, and initial conditions, necessitating a more robust approach to constrain dark matter self-interactions in cluster mergers.
AI.method: The paper introduces a novel method using the ratio of shock-to-shock distance traced by double radio relics to halo-to-halo distance, serving as a merger chronometer that is largely independent of self-interaction effects in shock propagation, enabling direct constraints on SICS while marginalizing over variables such as mass, viewing angle, collision parameters, and gas profile.
AI.result: By applying the shock-to-shock distance ratio method to a sample of eleven cluster mergers with symmetric double radio relics, the study delivers a robust 68% confidence upper limit on the SICS, fully incorporating uncertainties across multiple parameters, marking the first such fully marginalized constraint from cluster collisions.
AI.conclusion: The study establishes an upper limit on the self-interaction cross-section of dark matter (SICS) of sigma/m < 0.22 cm^2/g by analyzing merging galaxy clusters with double radio relics, successfully accounting for several key uncertainties.

title: Deep Learning galaxy cluster's structural parameters from Weak Lensing observations
summary: Galaxy clusters are the most massive gravitationally bound structures in the Universe and key probes of cosmic evolution. The large data volume expected from upcoming surveys requires efficient automated analysis methods for tens of thousands of clusters. We present a study using Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) to infer cluster structural parameters from weak gravitational lensing observations. Three architectures (VGG-Net, Inception-v4, Inception-ResNet-v2) were implemented in PyTorch and trained on 75,000 synthetic reduced shear maps generated with MOKA, simulating galaxy clusters at $z = 0.25$. The networks simultaneously predict five parameters: virial mass, NFW concentrations, substructure count, and substructure mass fraction. Tests on 5000 clusters show high accuracy for primary properties. With realistic noise ($n_{\rm gal}=30$, $σ_ε=0.3$), mass predictions remain robust (RMS $\sim 1.02 \times 10^{14}$ M$_\odot$/h, $\sim20$\% deviation). Concentration estimates are stable, with VGG-22 achieving the lowest RMS. Substructure properties are more challenging, with systematic underestimation across models. Comparison with traditional shear profile fitting shows improved CNN performance. VGG-22 achieves near-unbiased mass estimates and significantly better concentration recovery, reducing systematic errors. These results demonstrate that CNNs provide an effective and scalable alternative to traditional methods, particularly suited for large survey datasets.[Abridged]

AI.tldr: This study demonstrates that CNNs trained on synthetic weak lensing data can accurately predict key structural parameters of galaxy clusters, outperforming traditional methods and offering a scalable solution for analyzing upcoming large survey datasets.
AI.motivation: The motivation is to develop efficient automated methods to analyze large volumes of galaxy cluster data from upcoming surveys, focusing on inferring cluster structural parameters from weak gravitational lensing observations.
AI.method: The paper implements and trains three Convolutional Neural Network architectures (VGG-Net, Inception-v4, Inception-ResNet-v2) in PyTorch on 75,000 synthetic reduced shear maps simulating galaxy clusters at redshift 0.25 to simultaneously predict five cluster parameters.
AI.result: CNN models showed high accuracy in predicting primary properties such as virial mass and concentration from synthetic data, with VGG-22 providing near-unbiased mass and improved concentration estimates compared to traditional shear profile fitting; substructure properties were less accurately predicted with systematic underestimation.
AI.conclusion: CNNs represent an effective and scalable alternative to traditional methods for inferring galaxy cluster parameters from weak lensing data, particularly suited for large survey datasets due to improved accuracy and robustness under realistic noise conditions.

title: Towards a measurement of the primordial helium isotope ratio
comment: 21 pages, 5 figures, Accepted for publication in the Astrophysical Journal
summary: We report the discovery of two metastable neutral helium (He I*) absorbers in the Milky Way, and use the upgraded CRyogenic InfraRed Echelle Spectrograph on the Very Large Telescope to determine the helium isotope ratio, $^{3}$He/$^{4}$He, along these sightlines. We have also obtained deeper observations of a third sightline to report a $\lesssim4\%$ precision measure of $^{3}$He/$^{4}$He in the Orion Nebula. These data have allowed us to place a $2σ$ limit on the time-variability of He I* absorption in the Orion nebula, ${\rm d}\log_{10} [N({\rm He\,I}^{*})/{\rm cm}^{-2}]/{\rm d}t\leq7.2\times10^{-4}~{\rm dex~yr}^{-1}$ ($<0.17\%~{\rm yr}^{-1}$), suggesting that these absorbers are in radiative equilibrium. We compute new galactic chemical evolution models of the Milky Way, and use our observations to infer the primordial helium isotope ratio and a scaling factor for the yields reported by nucleosynthesis calculations. Based on the data and models that we report here, we infer a best-fit value ($^{3}$He/$^{4}$He)$_{\rm P}=(1.15^{+0.24}_{-0.21})\times10^{-4}$, which agrees with Big Bang nucleosynthesis calculations that assume the Standard Model of particle physics in combination with the baryon density inferred from the cosmic microwave background temperature fluctuations. We infer the stellar yield scale relative to the solar metallicity, $y/Z_{\odot}=2.12^{+0.31}_{-0.29}$, which is somewhat higher than previously found. Finally, we note that the forthcoming extremely large telescopes are poised to determine $^{3}$He/$^{4}$He in more metal-poor environments, to secure a model-independent determination of the primordial value.

AI.tldr: This study measures helium isotope ratios in the Milky Way using advanced spectroscopy and modeling, confirming primordial values consistent with the Standard Model and highlighting higher stellar yields; upcoming telescopes will enhance these measurements further.
AI.motivation: To determine the helium isotope ratio in the Milky Way and refine models of primordial helium abundance and stellar yields through new observations and chemical evolution models.
AI.method: Discovered metastable neutral helium absorbers using the upgraded CRyogenic InfraRed Echelle Spectrograph on the Very Large Telescope; obtained precise measurements of $^{3}$He/$^{4}$He ratios along multiple sightlines including the Orion Nebula; computed galactic chemical evolution models to interpret observations.
AI.result: Measured $^{3}$He/$^{4}$He ratio in the Orion Nebula with $	extless 4\%$ precision; set a 2σ upper limit on the time-variability of He I* absorption suggesting radiative equilibrium; inferred primordial helium isotope ratio $(1.15^{+0.24}_{-0.21})\times10^{-4}$ consistent with Big Bang nucleosynthesis and cosmic microwave background data; found stellar yield scaling factor $y/Z_{} = 2.12^{+0.31}_{-0.29}$ higher than prior estimates.
AI.conclusion: The inferred primordial helium isotope ratio agrees with Standard Model Big Bang nucleosynthesis predictions, and the higher stellar yield scale informs galactic chemical evolution; future extremely large telescopes will improve isotope measurements in metal-poor environments for model-independent primordial helium determination.

title: Correspondence between a decaying dark matter sector scenario and scalar field model
summary: We explore the theoretical viability of modeling a decaying dark matter sector through a unified scalar field approach. Using exact analytical solutions of the Friedmann constraints, we map the fluid phenomenology onto a scalar field potential. Our analysis reveals that physical viability, specifically the existence of a well-defined potential minimum; inevitably forces the dark energy equation of state into the phantom domain. To resolve the kinetic pathologies at late times, we propose reinterpreting the framework within a complex scenario, mapping the imaginary transition to the angular dynamics of a $U(1)$ phase. This mapping naturally yields an ultra-light mass scale of $m_φ\sim 10^{-33} \ \text{eV}$, classifying the model as a unified dark fluid. Finally, we employ a dynamical approach to study the effects of non-minimal coupling, proving that the phantom-dominated epoch acts as a stable, late-time cosmic attractor in this kind of cosmological scenario.

AI.tldr: The paper demonstrates that a unified scalar field model for decaying dark matter requires phantom dark energy behavior, which can be stabilized by recasting the model into a complex field framework, resulting in a unified dark fluid with an ultra-light mass and a stable late-time cosmic attractor.
AI.motivation: To investigate the viability of modeling decaying dark matter through a unified scalar field framework addressing issues in dark energy behavior.
AI.method: Exact analytical solutions of Friedmann constraints to map fluid phenomenology onto a scalar field potential, followed by a complex scalar field reinterpretation and dynamical system analysis including non-minimal coupling.
AI.result: Physical viability requires the dark energy equation of state to enter the phantom domain; reinterpreting the scalar field as complex resolves kinetic pathologies and leads to an ultra-light mass scale (~10^{-33} eV). The phantom-dominated epoch is shown to be a stable late-time attractor under non-minimal coupling.
AI.conclusion: A unified scalar field model of decay dark matter inevitably leads to phantom dark energy behavior, which can be consistently described by a complex scalar field framework yielding a unified dark fluid with stable late-time cosmology.

title: A Detailed View of the Large-Scale Sloshing Cold Front in RXJ2014.8-2430
comment: 11 pages, 13 figures, accepted for publication in MNRAS
summary: We analyze our new 144 ks deep Chandra observation of the sloshing cold front cluster RXJ2014.8-2430. Previous observations of RXJ2014.8-2430 with XMM-Newton shows evidence of a large scale, sloshing cold front around 800 kpc away from the cluster core. Previous shallow Chandra data also shows evidence of two younger cold fronts closer to the core. Our new deeper Chandra data allow us to analyze the fine, small scale structure of these three cold fronts. Using both beta model subtraction and Gaussian Gradient Magnitude filtering, we confirm the locations of the three cold fronts, as well as discover a large concave structure southeast of the cluster core near the outermost cold front, which could be a large Kelvin-Helmholtz instability or a gas cavity from AGN activity. Analyzing the three cold fronts, we measure the widths of the cold fronts and find them to be consistent with or lower than the Coulomb mean free paths within error, signifying that diffusion is suppressed across the cold fronts. If the concave feature is the inner rim of a cavity, we find that it has a radius in the range 200-330kpc, and would have $PV$ values in the range of $5.7 \times 10^{60}$ - $2.7 \times 10^{61}$ erg. These values would make it consistent with the some of the most powerful bubbles observed.

AI.tldr: Deep Chandra observations of RXJ2014.8-2430 confirm three cold fronts, reveal a large concave structure that may be a powerful AGN-driven cavity or instability, with suppressed diffusion across cold fronts and energetics consistent with some of the most powerful bubbles seen in clusters.
AI.motivation: To analyze the fine, small scale structure of cold fronts in the sloshing cold front cluster RXJ2014.8-2430 using deeper Chandra observations, extending previous XMM-Newton and shallow Chandra studies.
AI.method: Utilized a 144 ks deep Chandra observation combined with beta model subtraction and Gaussian Gradient Magnitude filtering to identify and study the cold fronts and surrounding structures in the cluster.
AI.result: Confirmed three cold fronts at different scales, identified a large concave structure southeast of the cluster core potentially representing a Kelvin-Helmholtz instability or AGN-driven gas cavity, measured cold front widths consistent with suppressed diffusion, and estimated the cavity's energetics to be among the most powerful observed bubbles.
AI.conclusion: The deep Chandra data reveal detailed cold front structures in RXJ2014.8-2430, suggesting diffusion suppression and possible AGN activity influencing the cluster environment through large-scale cavities or instabilities.

title: Measuring $fσ_8$ and BAO scale in the Local Universe: a joint real and redshift space analysis from CosmicFlows-4++
summary: The large-scale clustering of galaxies encodes both geometric and dynamical information about the Universe. The Baryon Acoustic Oscillations (BAO) phenomenon provides a standard ruler that constrains the cosmic expansion history, while Redshift Space Distortions (RSD) probe the growth of structure through the peculiar velocity field. In this work, we present a joint analysis of BAO and growth rate parameter, $fσ_{8}$, in the Local Universe out to $z = 0.1$, using the $65,331$ galaxy distances of CosmicFlows-4++ database. A distinctive property of this catalogue is the availability of real space galaxy positions in addition to the redshift space coordinates. Fitting an empirical model to the measurements we obtain $r_{\rm{BAO}}^{\rm{real}} = 132\pm 8\,h^{-1}\,{\rm Mpc}$ in real space, and $r_{\rm{BAO}}^{z} = 139 \pm 7\,h^{-1}\,{\rm Mpc}$ in redshift space, at redshift $z = 0.07$. Modeling the enhancement of the correlation function within the Kaiser formalism, we derive a constraint on the growth rate parameter $fσ_8 = 0.344 \pm 0.105$. This analysis demonstrates how the combination of real and redshift space clustering measurements enables a simultaneous probe of important observables of the large-scale structure. Their joint detection in the same dataset, therefore, provides a self consistent view of the structure and evolution of the Local Universe. This study may be used for consistency analyses of upcoming surveys, as DESI and 4MOST, that will also provide data in both real and redshift space.

AI.tldr: This paper uses the CosmicFlows-4++ galaxy catalogue's real and redshift space data to jointly measure BAO scale and growth rate in the Local Universe, providing consistent constraints on cosmic expansion and growth of structure at low redshift.
AI.motivation: Since galaxy clustering encodes geometric and dynamical cosmological information, the study aims to leverage the distinct advantage of having both real and redshift space galaxy positions to jointly constrain the cosmic expansion (via BAO) and growth of structure (via RSD) in the Local Universe.
AI.method: A joint analysis was performed on 65,331 galaxy distances up to redshift z=0.1, fitting an empirical model to BAO measurements in both real and redshift space, and applying the Kaiser formalism to model redshift space distortions and extract the growth rate parameter.
AI.result: Obtained BAO scale of 132±8 h⁻¹ Mpc in real space and 139±7 h⁻¹ Mpc in redshift space at z=0.07, and a growth rate parameter fσ_8=0.344±0.105, demonstrating the feasibility and consistency of joint BAO and RSD measurement in a single dataset.
AI.conclusion: The study successfully demonstrates that combining real and redshift space clustering measurements from the CosmicFlows-4++ database allows for simultaneous constraints on BAO scale and growth rate parameter in the Local Universe, providing a self-consistent probe of large-scale structure.

title: Random Polarization Position Angle Behaviors across Bursts of Repeating Fast Radio Bursts
comment: 16 pages, 8 figures. Submitted to The Astrophysical Journal
summary: Fast radio bursts (FRBs), highly polarized, mostly have a nearly constant polarization position angle (PA) during each burst. Their PAs are observed to vary from burst to burst, with the statistical properties remaining stable across different observation sessions. We found that the intrinsic PAs of repeating FRBs are approximately Gaussian distributed, suggesting that the emission likely originates from a localized region within the neutron star's magnetosphere. A periodicity search of the PA time series using the Lomb-Scargle periodogram reveals no credible periodic signal in the period range from 10 ms to $10^7$ ms, and similar analyses of several active observations also yield null detections. We interpret these properties by extending the rotating vector model to include a dynamically evolving magnetosphere, in which the effective magnetic axis varies from burst to burst due to stochastic perturbations. In this framework, the observed PA distributions can naturally arise from geometric projection effects, and the absence of periodicity reflects the random wandering of the magnetic axis within a confined region. This scenario provides a natural explanation for both repeating and apparently non-repeating FRBs.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes FRB polarization angles, finds intrinsic Gaussian distribution and no periodicity, and explains these via a rotating vector model with a stochastic, evolving magnetosphere, unifying repeating and non-repeating FRB behavior.
AI.motivation: To understand the polarization position angle properties of fast radio bursts (FRBs) and their emission origin.
AI.method: Analyzed polarization position angles (PAs) of repeating FRBs; performed periodicity searches on PA time series using Lomb-Scargle periodogram; extended the rotating vector model to a dynamically evolving magnetosphere with stochastic perturbations to explain observations.
AI.result: Intrinsic PAs of repeating FRBs follow an approximately Gaussian distribution, no credible periodicity detected in PA variations, and the extended rotating vector model explains observed PA distributions and absence of periodicity by random wandering of the magnetic axis.
AI.conclusion: The observed stable yet randomly varying polarization angles of FRBs suggest emission from a localized region within a neutron star magnetosphere with a dynamically evolving magnetic axis, providing a unified explanation for both repeating and non-repeating FRBs.

title: A consistent formulation of stochastic inflation I: Non-Markovian effects and issues beyond linear perturbations
summary: We investigate the origin of non-Markovianity in stochastic inflation and its implications for nonlinear perturbation theory. In the Schwinger--Keldysh formulation, the noise terms sourcing the infrared (IR) Langevin equations are determined by ultraviolet (UV) modes evolving on top of the stochastic IR background. Since the UV-mode evolution generally depends on the past history of the IR sector, the resulting stochastic dynamics is intrinsically non-Markovian. Working perturbatively, we derive the UV-mode solutions up to second order and decompose the corresponding noise contributions into two parts. The first is a ``deterministic'' contribution, generated by the functional Taylor expansion of the first-order UV solution around the background trajectory. The second is a genuinely ``stochastic'' contribution, originating from terms in the UV-mode equations that are quadratic in the noise variables and are usually neglected in the standard formulation of stochastic inflation. Under this conventional truncation, the deterministic contribution reduces to a Markovian correction in attractor backgrounds, whereas it could become history dependent in non-attractor phases and gives rise to non-Markovian terms involving integrals over first-order IR perturbations. We finally show that the stochastic contribution is of the same perturbative order as the deterministic one, which indicate that the conventional truncation is generically inconsistent and quadratic-noise terms may be required for a consistent treatment of nonlinear perturbations in stochastic inflation. Our analysis clarifies the perturbative structure of non-Markovianity and provides the basis for a systematic treatment of quadratic-noise effects beyond the standard formulation.

AI.tldr: This paper reveals that non-Markovian noise in stochastic inflation arises from UV-mode history dependence on IR backgrounds and shows that commonly neglected quadratic-noise terms are crucial for consistent nonlinear perturbation theory, challenging standard truncation practices.
AI.motivation: To understand the origin of non-Markovianity in stochastic inflation and its consequences for nonlinear perturbation theory.
AI.method: Use the Schwinger--Keldysh formalism to derive UV-mode solutions up to second order and decompose noise contributions into deterministic and stochastic parts, analyzing perturbative corrections and history dependence in different background phases.
AI.result: Identified that stochastic dynamics are intrinsically non-Markovian due to UV-mode dependence on IR history; deterministic noise terms reduce to Markovian corrections only in attractor backgrounds but induce non-Markovian effects in non-attractor phases; stochastic quadratic-noise contributions are of the same order as deterministic ones, indicating conventional truncation neglecting them is inconsistent.
AI.conclusion: The conventional truncation in stochastic inflation neglecting quadratic-noise terms is generically inconsistent, requiring inclusion of these terms for a consistent perturbative treatment of nonlinear perturbations; the work clarifies the perturbative structure of non-Markovianity and lays groundwork for systematic treatment beyond standard formulations.

title: Maximal mass of neutron stars constrained by neutron star observations
comment: Accepted for publication in Journal of Subatomic Particles and Cosmology
summary:
We investigate constraints on the high-density equation of state (EOS) of neutron star matter by analyzing the probability distributions of the endpoints of mass-radius M(R) sequences within a Bayesian weighting framework. Starting from two representative hadronic baseline EOSs, SFHo and DD2, matched at higher densities to an extended linear sigma model description and constrained to approach perturbative QCD (pQCD) results, we construct families of causal hybrid EOSs spanning a broad range of stiffness at supranuclear densities. Observational constraints from the binary neutron-star merger GW170817, mass-radius measurements from the Neutron Star Interior Composition Explorer (NICER), and candidate low-mass and mass-gap compact objects are incorporated through Bayesian likelihood weighting. This approach allows us to determine probability distributions for the maximum neutron-star mass M$_{\rm TOV}$ and the corresponding radius R$_{\rm TOV}$, i.e., the endpoints of the M(R) sequences.
  We find that the maximum-mass distributions are largely determined by observational constraints and show only weak sensitivity to the choice of baseline EOS, favoring values around 2.2-2.3 M$_\odot$ when the most robust constraints are applied. In contrast, the corresponding radius distributions exhibit a stronger dependence on the underlying hadronic EOS, with typical preferred values near $12\pm 1$ km. Additional tidal-deformability constraints further restrict the allowed parameter space and disfavor very stiff EOS realizations when interpreted together with the possible mass-gap neutron-star candidate. Our results demonstrate that endpoint distributions of M(R) sequences provide a sensitive and complementary diagnostic for constraining the high-density behavior of the neutron-star EOS within a multimessenger Bayesian framework.

AI.tldr: This paper employs Bayesian analysis of mass-radius endpoint distributions from hybrid EOS models and astrophysical data (GW170817, NICER) to constrain neutron star maximum mass (~2.2-2.3 M☉) and radius (~12 km), highlighting sensitivity to hadronic EOS and tidal deformability effects.
AI.motivation: To constrain the high-density equation of state (EOS) of neutron star matter using observational data and theoretical models.
AI.method: Construct causal hybrid EOSs matched to hadronic baselines SFHo and DD2 and extended linear sigma model with pQCD constraints; analyze M(R) endpoint distributions within a Bayesian framework using data from GW170817, NICER, and candidate compact objects.
AI.result: Maximum neutron-star mass distributions are constrained around 2.2-2.3 solar masses, weakly dependent on baseline EOS; radius distributions depend more on hadronic EOS (~12±1 km); tidal deformability restricts very stiff EOS scenarios.
AI.conclusion: Endpoint distributions of mass-radius sequences effectively constrain the high-density neutron-star EOS, serving as a sensitive diagnostic tool in a multimessenger Bayesian framework.

title: DESI and Gravitational Wave Constraints Challenge Quintessential α-Attractor Inflation
summary: Quintessential inflation models provide a framework that simultaneously describes inflation and dynamical dark energy, the latter of which has recently received growing support from DESI observations. A distinctive feature of these models is the kination phase after inflation, which enhances primordial gravitational waves at high frequencies. In this work, we study a class of alpha-attractor quintessential inflation models using a fully numerical approach that follows the scalar-field evolution from inflation to the dark-energy-dominated era, allowing us to compute with high precision both the dynamics of dark energy and the primordial gravitational wave spectrum. Using the latest observational data, including DESI and ACT, we constrain the model parameters and show that the model becomes disfavored once constraints from the gravitational-wave contribution to the effective number of relativistic degrees of freedom, Δ Neff, are included. This is because the model predicts a scalar spectral index ns that becomes too small to remain consistent with observations when the gravitational-wave abundance is constrained to stay below the Δ Neff bound. Finally, we present the resulting primordial gravitational wave power spectrum computed using our constrained parameter values, which highlights prospects for detection by future CMB B-mode experiments at low frequencies and by gravitational-wave interferometer experiments at high frequencies.

AI.tldr: This study numerically analyzes alpha-attractor quintessential inflation models with kination, constrains them using latest cosmological and gravitational-wave data, finds observational tension limiting their viability, but highlights potential primordial gravitational wave signals detectable by future experiments.
AI.motivation: To investigate a class of alpha-attractor quintessential inflation models that unify inflation and dynamical dark energy while accounting for recent observational data and the characteristic kination phase enhancing high-frequency primordial gravitational waves.
AI.method: A fully numerical approach tracking scalar-field evolution from inflation through to dark-energy domination, enabling precise computation of dark energy dynamics and the primordial gravitational wave spectrum; constraints on model parameters were applied using latest observational data including DESI, ACT, and gravitational-wave bounds on ΔNeff.
AI.result: The model parameters constrained by observations show that the alpha-attractor quintessential inflation models become disfavored when gravitational-wave contributions to ΔNeff are included, as this forces the scalar spectral index ns to values inconsistent with data; nevertheless, the predicted primordial gravitational wave spectrum suggests detectability prospects by future CMB B-mode and gravitational-wave interferometer experiments.
AI.conclusion: Alpha-attractor quintessential inflation models incorporating kination phases predict enhanced high-frequency primordial gravitational waves but face tension with observational constraints, especially from gravitational-wave contributions to ΔNeff, limiting their viability despite promising detection prospects.

title: Multi-messenger Constraints on a Primordial Black Hole Origin of the KM3-230213A Event
comment: Contribution to the 2026 Very High Energy Phenomena in the Universe session of the 60th Rencontres de Moriond. Included determination of DM fraction compatible with the KM3NeT event in a diffuse PBH population scenario
summary: Black holes are expected to end their lifetime in a burst of Hawking radiation, emitting all Standard Model particles at ultra-high energies. The evaporation of a nearby primordial black hole (PBH) has been proposed as an explanation for the high-energy neutrino-like event reported by KM3NeT. Such a scenario requires the source to be extremely close to Earth, implying detectable gamma-ray and cosmic-ray emission. Accounting for the time-dependent field of view of gamma-ray observatories, we find that current experiments should have observed a pre-burst signal, while neutrino telescopes would also detect lower-energy events before the burst. The absence of such multimessenger signals strongly disfavors a PBH origin of the KM3-230213A event in the minimal 4D Schwarzschild scenario.

AI.tldr: This study examines whether a nearby primordial black hole could explain a high-energy neutrino event but finds that the lack of accompanying gamma-ray and neutrino precursors rules out this scenario.
AI.motivation: To investigate whether the high-energy neutrino-like event observed by KM3NeT could be explained by the evaporation of a nearby primordial black hole (PBH).
AI.method: Analyzed the expected multimessenger signals including gamma-rays, cosmic-rays, and neutrinos from PBH evaporation, accounting for the time-dependent field of view of gamma-ray observatories and neutrino telescopes.
AI.result: Current experiments should have detected precursor signals in gamma-rays and lower-energy neutrinos before the burst event, but no such signals were observed.
AI.conclusion: The absence of multimessenger precursor signals strongly disfavors the minimal 4D Schwarzschild PBH evaporation scenario as the origin of the KM3-230213A high-energy neutrino event.

authors: the LSST Dark Energy Science Collaboration
title: Optimization of Weak Lensing Lightcone Simulations for Higher-Order Statistics in the LSST era
comment: 48 pages, 19 figures. We publicly release Pollux, the lightcone-construction framework developed for this project: https://github.com/LSSTDESC/pollux
summary: We present a framework for generating lightcone simulations tailored to the analysis of Stage-IV cosmic shear data using Higher-Order Statistics (HOS). We revisit key design choices from previous simulation campaigns and re-optimize several internal parameters, benchmarking accuracy through changes in $χ^2$ of cosmic shear statistics under survey conditions mimicking 10 years of observations from the Legacy Survey of Space and Time (LSST). We find that discretizing the lightcone uniformly in scale factor yields higher accuracy than commonly adopted schemes such as uniform spacing in redshift or comoving distance. While $N_{\rm part} = 1024^3$ simulation particles (corresponding to a mass resolution of $m_{\rm part} = 2.08\times10^{10}M_\odot$) is sufficient to model two-point statistics up to $\ell = 5000$, we observed significant instabilities on our full suite of HOS as the number of mass shells used in the lightcone construction, $N_{\rm shells}$, is varied. In contrast, simulations with $N_{\rm part} = 2048^3$ particles ($m_{\rm part} = 2.60\times10^{9}M_\odot$) robustly reproduce all statistics considered. In this higher-resolution configuration, $N_{\rm shells}$ can be reduced to $\sim50$ with only minor deviations, no larger than $0.1-0.3σ$ relative to our highest-resolution case ($N_{\rm shells}\sim100$). This has been explicitly verified through a comparison between our fiducial lightcone production mode based on slicing particle snapshots and an exact lightcone mode where individual particle trajectories are solved for at runtime. We further show that the particle density per pixel can be downsampled by a significant amount for $z>1.5$, saving large computational resources with no impact on the resulting statistics. These results guide the design of upcoming simulation campaigns geared towards forward-modeling and emulation-based analyses of Stage-IV data.

AI.tldr: This paper optimizes lightcone simulation parameters for Stage-IV cosmic shear analysis, finding that uniform scale factor spacing and higher particle resolution (~2048³) ensure stable Higher-Order Statistics. Reducing mass shells and particle density at high redshift lowers computation without sacrificing statistical accuracy, guiding efficient future simulation campaigns.
AI.motivation: To optimize lightcone simulations for analyzing Stage-IV cosmic shear data using Higher-Order Statistics (HOS) under realistic survey conditions mimicking 10 years of LSST observations.
AI.method: Revisiting and re-optimizing simulation design choices including discretization of the lightcone in scale factor, particle number, and number of mass shells; benchmarking accuracy via changes in χ² of cosmic shear statistics; performing comparisons between slicing particle snapshots and exact lightcone construction modes; downsampling particle density at high redshift.
AI.result: Uniform scale factor discretization improves accuracy; lower particle numbers (1024³) insufficient for stable HOS, higher resolution (2048³) yields robust reproduction of all statistics; reducing number of mass shells to ~50 causes minor deviations; verified equivalence of fiducial and exact lightcone methods; particle downsampling beyond z>1.5 reduces computational cost without affecting statistics.
AI.conclusion: Careful optimization of simulation parameters, especially particle resolution and lightcone construction, enables accurate forward-modeling of cosmic shear HOS for Stage-IV surveys like LSST while reducing computational demand through strategic downsampling and shell number reduction.

title: A bright wideband radio burst from the isolated neutron star 2XMM J104608.7$-$594306
summary: We present the discovery of a second coherent radio burst from the thermally emitting neutron star 2XMM J104608.7$-$594306 in our follow-up observations with the Murriyang Ultra-Wideband Low receiver. This burst shows complex morphology with multiple components and wideband emission spanning from 704 to 4032MHz. We measured a steep spectral index of $α=-2.18\pm0.16$. Our polarimetric analysis demonstrates that the burst is highly polarised with a linear and circular polarisation fraction of 54% and 22%, respectively. We identified an orthogonal jump in the polarisation position angles of the burst, resembling those seen in radio pulsars. We compared this burst with the first radio burst detected from the source with MeerKAT. These two bursts detected in a total of 40 hours on source with MeerKAT and Murriyang, combined, show that 2XMM J104608.7$-$594306 can emit sporadic radio emission with luminosity jumps comparable to those seen in the bright bursts from SGR 1935+2154. This suggests that previously thought radio-quiet neutron stars such as X-ray dim isolated neutron stars and central compact objects could exhibit rare radio bursting activity.

AI.tldr: The paper reports the discovery of a second coherent radio burst from neutron star 2XMM J104608.7$-$594306, showing complex, highly polarised emission across a wide frequency range, indicating that some neutron stars thought to be radio-quiet can produce rare, bright radio bursts similar to known magnetar bursts.
AI.motivation: Investigate the rare radio emission activity from neutron stars previously considered radio-quiet, such as X-ray dim isolated neutron stars and central compact objects.
AI.method: Follow-up observations using the Murriyang Ultra-Wideband Low receiver and comparison with earlier MeerKAT data, including polarimetric analysis and spectral measurements.
AI.result: Detection of a second coherent radio burst exhibiting complex morphology, wideband emission from 704 to 4032 MHz, steep spectral index, and high polarisation with orthogonal position angle jumps. Both bursts indicate sporadic radio emission with luminosity jumps comparable to bright bursts from SGR 1935+2154.
AI.conclusion: Neutron stars previously classified as radio-quiet can exhibit rare, sporadic radio bursts, suggesting a broader range of radio emission activity among thermally emitting neutron stars.

title: Upstream neutrino production and delayed jet emission in the blazar GB6 J1542+6129
comment: 4 pages, 2 figures, submitted to A&A Letters. Comments welcome
summary: We investigate the physical origin and location of high-energy neutrino emission in active galactic nuclei (AGN) using the blazar GB6 J1542+6129 as a case study, testing whether neutrinos are produced in compact regions near the black hole or in parsec-scale jets. This question is central to understanding the conditions under which hadronic processes become efficient in AGN environments. We perform a multimessenger analysis combining ~17 years of Fermi-LAT gamma-ray data, including a 5% adaptively binned light curve and Bayesian block decomposition, with ~14 years of VLBI/MOJAVE observations to derive the Doppler factor evolution of the radio core. These are compared to the temporal properties of a suspected IceCube neutrino flare with a duration of $147^{+110}_{-25}$ days. We find that the suspected neutrino flare precedes both a gamma-ray flare and a pronounced increase in the VLBI core Doppler factor by ~1 year. This delay is consistent with the propagation time of a disturbance from the central engine to the 15GHz radio core. The duration of the post-flare gamma-ray activity is similar to that of the neutrino flare. The broadband gamma-ray spectral energy distributions remain consistent in shape across the full, flare, and post-flare intervals, indicating stable particle acceleration conditions. The temporal ordering favors neutrino production upstream of the VLBI core. GB6 J1542+6129 provides evidence for spatially separated neutrino and gamma-ray/radio emission regions in AGN. The observations are consistent with a disturbance-driven, multi-zone scenario in which neutrinos are produced in a compact, photon-rich region near the central engine, while the same disturbance later enhances Doppler-boosted leptonic emission at the parsec-scale VLBI core. These results demonstrate the power of multimessenger observations in constraining the origin of astrophysical neutrinos.
